Experience Aviva

Together, we are Aviva.

Our values of Care, Commitment, Community, and Confidence guide how we show up for each other and our customers. At Aviva Canada, we put people first through a culture built on inclusion, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

The Opportunit
y

The VP Technology and Transformation Risk is a senior member of the Canada Risk function, responsible for providing independent second line oversight and challenge across Technology, Data, Cyber, AI and Transformation risks. The role supports the effective management of these risks across Aviva Canada, helping ensure business objectives can be delivered within the Aviva Canada’s risk appetite framework and regulatory expectations.

The role partners closely with Group and local stakeholders to provide independent risk advice, oversight and challenge, supporting the ongoing development of risk management practices and frameworks across technology and transformation activities.

Risks within the role holder's remit include Cyber Risk, Data Risk, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Emerging Technology Risk and other IT risks.

The role leads specialist risk teams and works closely with colleagues across Risk, Technology, Operations and Transformation functions to provide insight on emerging risks, monitor risk exposures, and support consistent application of Aviva Canada and Group policies and standards.

What You'll Do

Provide independent second line oversight and challenge of Technology, Data, Cyber, AI and Transformation risks across the Group.
Partner with senior leaders within Technology, Operations, Customer & Marketing and Transformation functions to support effective risk management and informed decision-making.
Monitor and assess technology and transformation risk exposures, providing insights and recommendations to senior management and risk committees.
Support the development, maintenance and implementation of Aviva Canada and Group risk frameworks, policies, standards and risk appetite measures relating to Technology, Data, Cyber, AI and Transformation risks
Contribute to risk reporting and analysis provided to Board Risk Committee and Executive Committees as required.
Provide independent review and challenge of significant technology and transformation initiatives, including major change programs and strategic investments
Support regulatory engagement activities and the provision of evidence relating to Technology, Cyber, Data and Transformation risk management practices.
Oversee the identification and assessment of technology concentration, critical dependency and third-party risks across key platforms, suppliers and services.
Monitor emerging technology developments and evolving risk trends, providing thought leadership and practical guidance to business stakeholders
Promote consistency in the application of risk policies, frameworks and methodologies across Aviva Canada.
Lead and develop specialist risk teams, creating a high-performance culture and strengthening risk expertise across Technology and Transformation disciplines.
Contribute to the development and execution of the wider Risk Function strategy and priorities.
Support continuous improvement initiatives across the Risk Function, including the adoption of data, technology and agile ways of working.

What You'll Bring

A degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Business, or a related field.
15+ years of experience in data governance, data management, analytics, or a related discipline.
Relevant Insurance qualifications and/or Risk professional qualifications, CRM, CRMP, FRM, PRM or equivalent
Significant experience in enterprise risk management within a regulated financial services or insurance environment, including application of the Three Lines of Defense model
Deep expertise in Technology, Cyber, Data, AI, Operational Resilience and Third-Party Risk oversight and governance
Proven oversight of large-scale transformation and change programs, including complex initiatives with multiple stakeholders and dependencies
Experience partnering with senior executives (CIO, COO, business leaders) and influencing strategic decisions
Strong people leadership experience, including building, leading and developing high-performing specialist teams
Experience engaging with regulators, audit functions, executive committees and board-level stakeholders on risk matters.

What You'll Get

Competitive executive compensation package, including annual incentive opportunities.
Comprehensive pension and retirement savings programs.
Flexible hybrid work model.
Industry-leading health and wellness benefits.
Professional development and executive leadership growth opportunities.
Inclusive employee resource groups and diversity initiatives.
Volunteer opportunities and community impact programs.
Competitive vacation and wellness offerings.

jobs.title: Director of Product Management, Data Integrations
jobs.description:
Movable Ink scales content personalization for marketers through data-activated content generation and AI decisioning. The world’s most innovative brands rely on Movable Ink to maximize revenue, simplify workflow and boost marketing agility. Headquartered in New York City with close to 600 employees, Movable Ink serves its global client base with operations throughout North America, Central America, Europe, Australia, and Japan. We’re looking for a Director, Product Management to partner closely with Engineering to define and evolve how data flows across our platform. You’ll lead a team of Senior Product Managers responsible for data workflows and third-party integrations while staying hands-on as a contributor and close partner to Engineering. You’ll have a broad view across our data and integrations ecosystem, connecting the dots between how data arrives from external platforms, how it’s shaped and made useful within our tools, and where it needs to go to power the personalization our customers depend on. You’ll also be a key point of contact for external vendor relationships and a visible, trusted partner to our Partnerships, Sales, and Customer Experience teams. The role reports to the Vice President of Product Management.

Responsibilities

Directly own product initiatives in the data ingestion and standardization space, partnering closely with engineering as a hands-on contributor
Maintain a unified roadmap across a portfolio that spans data ingestion and normalization, event collection and processing, data workflows and orchestration, third-party integrations, and data governance, ensuring investments across these areas connect to broader company priorities including AI, personalization, analytics, and reporting
Serve as a proactive partner to peer product teams who rely on the data platform, bringing them into roadmap decisions early, maintaining visibility into how this team's work affects their products, and contributing informed perspective on platform APIs and developer-facing integration surfaces
Lead, coach, and develop a team of senior product managers across data workflow and integrations domains, with an eye toward each person's distinct growth path
Serve as the senior point of contact for third-party vendor and partner relationships across technical and business development contacts
Support the team in maintaining an active integration pipeline and consistently launching net-new partners that meet adoption and reliability benchmarks
Stay ahead of the evolving marketing technology and data integration landscape, including emerging paradigms such as agentic platforms and Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Be a ruthless advocate for our customers in every interaction and decision

Qualifications

8+ years of product management experience, including people management of senior individual contributors
Deep experience with data products, including ingestion, transformation, normalization, or workflow, and genuine curiosity about how data moves through complex systems
Strong engineering partnership instincts, with fluency in data pipeline architecture, event streaming, ETL/ELT, and data warehouse design sufficient to engage credibly in architectural trade-off conversations
Experience with marketing technology ecosystems including ESPs, MSPs, CDPs, and CRMs, with familiarity with modern data stack technologies such as Snowflake, Kafka, dbt, or Airflow
Working knowledge of API design and developer-facing integration surfaces
A natural coach who can develop people along genuinely different growth paths
Skilled communicator across engineering, commercial, and external partner audiences

The base pay range for this position is $190,000 - $247,000/year, which can include additional bonus depending on the position ultimately offered, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits. The base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and serving on the Senior Management Team, the Interim Vice-President holds overall accountability for psychometrics and related data analysis, and leads PEBC’s enterprise data strategy, data analytics and business intelligence, data governance, and reporting. The role ensures the validity, reliability, fairness and defensibility of high-stakes national certification examinations, and positions data as a strategic asset informing decision-making across the organization.

Combining strategic leadership with deep technical authority, the Interim Vice-President advances psychometric and analytic practice through established and emerging methodologies, research and evidence-informed decision-making.

Own the reporting, dashboard and data-visualization environment, including self-serve business intelligence for senior leadership, the Board and stakeholders, underpinned by a governed single source of truth and semantic layer.
Champion a data strategy that treats assessment and operational data as a strategic asset, and advance analytics from descriptive and diagnostic reporting toward predictive and prescriptive capability.

Advise on psychometric and standard-setting decisions with high-stakes or policy-level impact, and on statistical and forensic findings related to testing irregularities.
Partner closely with executive peers in Assessments, Technology and Operations, and present psychometric results, validity evidence and recommendations to the Board's examinations committee.
Lead all HR matters for the Psychometrics and Data Analytics department, including recruitment, training, retention and performance management, along with annual business priorities, projects and budget.

Qualifications

PhD required, ideally in psychometrics or educational measurement, or in a closely related quantitative discipline such as statistics.

Substantial experience as a psychometrician in educational or psychological testing (typically eight or more years), including high-stakes assessment.
Strong expertise in psychometric methodologies, including standard setting, equating and scaling.
Experience leading or overseeing enterprise data strategy, data governance, data analytics and business intelligence/reporting.
Proven ability to design, conduct, interpret and present psychometric analyses and studies in high-stakes assessment contexts.
Strong data analysis and scientific-computing skills, and familiarity with business-intelligence and data-visualization tools.
Experience leveraging data science, machine learning or emerging AI tools to support measurement and analytics.
